ruleName: PASS boundary control. Government 2FA identity step: 'Sending verification code…' is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then the SAME region is overwritten in-place with '✓ Code sent to the mobile number ending 47. Enter it below.' (announced), and the OTP input is revealed. The end of the wait is announced by REPLACING the busy text, not by silently removing it — the correct 'Removal of status text' remediation.

ruleName: Team-workspace SaaS ('Helmsley Workspace') notification-preferences page: pressing 'Save preferences' reveals a green 'Preferences saved.' banner beside the button. The banner is wired aria-live='off' with aria-atomic='true', carries no role=status/alert/log and is not an <output>, so the live-region wiring looks present to a linter while the value 'off' tells assistive technology to ignore the update. Sighted users see the confirmation; screen-reader users hear nothing and cannot tell whether the save succeeded.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Clicking 'Save preferences' displays 'Preferences saved.' in a plain element with aria-live="off", meaning the status message is never announced to assistive technology.

ruleName: LMS reflective-essay editor (contenteditable) autosaves. A 'Saving your changes…' pill is announced in a top-bar role=status polite region on entry, then on success the pill is simply removed and the save-status area goes blank — no 'All changes saved' replacement. Sighted users infer success from the pill vanishing; AT users hear 'Saving…' then permanent silence and cannot tell if the draft saved before the deadline.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The autosave status region is correctly wired and announces 'Saving your changes…' when populated, but silently empties at 2205 ms with no follow-up outcome message, so AT users never learn the save completed.

The ticker is a present, valid live region wired aria-live=assertive, and a setInterval re-prices NDX/SPX/BTC every 2 seconds. ruleName: Government unemployment-benefits wizard, 'certify your claim' step. The user must read a long legal certification statement before checking the agree box. A secure-session region (present, valid) is wired aria-live=polite; when the 30-second expiry countdown is injected, polite politeness queues it behind the long statement the screen reader is still narrating, so it is heard only after the session has already ended and the answers are discarded. A blocking, time-critical countdown must be assertive.

ruleName: Restaurant reservation widget: 'Checking availability…' plus a spinner is announced in a role=status polite region on entry, then on success the busy region is emptied and a previously-disabled 'Reserve this table' button is enabled (its label unchanged). Sighted users read the spinner vanishing + the greyed button lighting up as 'a table is available'; AT users hear 'Checking availability…' then silence, with no 'Available — you can book' status and only a bare disabled→enabled control flip.

ruleName:
Hospital patient-portal 'Refill prescription' screen (F103, muted-when-it-matters). The refill-outcome region

is set to aria-live="off" by a backwards, on-by-default 'Focus mode' toggle, so the consequential 'Refill request FAILED - requires prescriber re-authorization' message is written into a silenced region. ruleName: PASS boundary: a bank sign-in verification screen with correct urgency-to-politeness mapping in BOTH directions. (A) A 60-second one-time-code expiry that BLOCKS sign-in is correctly wired role=alert (assertive) so the user hears the deadline in time. (B) A trivial 'Devices currently signed in: N' badge updating every few seconds is correctly wired aria-live=polite so it never interrupts, and carries an on/off toggle exactly as SCR14 prescribes for nonessential alerts. Politeness matches meaning and cadence, so the page passes.
